comparison: Two layouts of the same generated fwp task program: a test-only reconstruction of the preceding heap-embedded libc context versus the candidate context in existing child stacks and root static storage. No C/Rust comparison.
workload: 32 tasks each yield and add one to inputs 0 through 31, then await results, sum and print 528. Both layouts agree with raw interpretation. Nine fresh processes per layout, ARC/tracing mode and C O0/O2 on each host.
scope: Managed allocation requests, requested bytes, effective retains, peak/final allocator charge, task/context sizeof, actual ELF sections/load segments, checkpoint peak resident memory and complete process elapsed time are distinct measurements. Context bytes move into stack/static storage; they do not disappear. ELF segment memory excludes page alignment and is not RSS.
correctness: Saved root/child register images independently retain live values through collection; omitting their roots exits 191/192 at O0/O2. Native root-image teardown omission exits 193. Separate verification binaries check alignment, usable stack bounds, completed context-pointer clearing and teardown. Task-free programs do not initialize or clear saved root state; deliberately clearing it exits 197. Library unload tests include omitted root-image clearing, and static-memory tests execute with strace available. Task cancellation, scope ownership and service-response cleanup pass.
limitations: Short process samples include startup, instrumentation, output capture and teardown. VmHWM is observed after task teardown and before final allocator/process exit; it includes shared mappings and is not private physical memory. No isolated switch latency, cache benefit, statistical significance, general speed improvement, zero ARC or elimination of GC is claimed. Full final-head production acceptance is separate.

excluded_run.reason: Both test jobs passed, but candidate-only verification assertions also executed in timed binaries. Those timings are excluded from the matched comparison.

service_comparison.scope: The existing nine-case, 72-call service fixture provides a second workload. It measures managed allocations/retains after listener readiness. Root/static storage, task stack pools, allocator metadata and OS buffers are outside these counters. The live listener is identified by its actual allocations; every other managed owner must finish. This is a layout/count comparison, not a matched process-time measurement; preserve observed peak variability.

reproduction: Dispatch numerics.yml with suite=task-contexts and native_runner=all at source_revision. Each native artifact contains process samples, source, binary, symbols, disassembly, section sizes and toolchain/host metadata.

process_measurements.comparison: Same generated fwp program, with either the preceding heap-embedded task context or the candidate stack-owned context. This is not a C/Rust comparison.
process_measurements.workload: 32 tasks each yield once and add one to inputs 0 through 31. Await every result, sum them, print 528 and tear down the runtime. Each repetition starts a new process.
process_measurements.memory_scope: Linux VmHWM from /proc/self/status at the post-task-teardown checkpoint, before final allocator/process exit. This is the peak resident memory observed up to that point, including startup, runtime, code, shared library mappings and stacks; not private physical memory or a guarantee about later exit work. Allocator counters and sizeof layouts are separate. The observation opens /proc after the counted region.
process_measurements.time_scope: Parent monotonic elapsed time around spawning and waiting for each complete child, including startup, output capture and teardown. These short processes do not isolate context-switch latency; ratios are observations for this workload, not a general speed claim.
process_measurements.ratio: Candidate divided by preceding layout: 1 means equal, below 1 means less, above 1 means more. Raw samples and ranges preserve variability; no significance claim.
process_measurements.flags: fwp emission at O1; generated C at the named O0/O2, -std=gnu11 -ffp-contract=off -w and normal runtime links. Measurement settings explicitly disable tracing collections and reuse verification and enable physical freeing.
process_measurements.instrumentation: Both variants use the same allocation-counting and final reporting hooks. Candidate-specific stack bounds, cleared pointers and root-image assertions execute in separate verification binaries, excluded from these measurements.
